A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VUF and Mechanistic Uncertainty Calibration study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-extraction, steering, hallucination-detection, and mitigation experiments on TriviaQA, NQ-Open, and PopQA.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds 70B-model evaluation, comparison methods, control experiments, and a failure case.

M1.justification: The specified VUF extraction rule changes from the raw difference of mean activations in v1 Equation 1 to an explicitly L2-normalized direction in v2 Equations 2–3. This changes the specified steering-vector scale. The detector and adaptive SU–VU intervention rule remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the underlying implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate closed-book short-form QA on TriviaQA, NQ-Open, and PopQA. The added model, controls, and case study remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds EigenScore to the SEP comparison in Table 2 and random-vector steering to Table 5. Existing uncertainty-based comparisons and SEP results are retained.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands to Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct as a generator, extends Qwen steering sweeps from ±1 to ±10, and adds overall hallucination rate alongside confident hallucination rate. New random-vector controls match intervention strength and vector-value range. These substantially extend the evaluation design; existing dataset splits and sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds random-direction controls testing whether mitigation specifically benefits from VUF steering, causal validation using the previously described ESU extraction method to address judge circularity, and a correctness-loss case study (Table 5, Appendix E.5/Figure 13, Appendix G.3). Qwen sensitivity testing is also extended. Existing transfer and alternative-score similarity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 2.3 newly reports MANOVA significance for the four response groups, with p-values below 0.0001. v1 presented the distributions without this test. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or error-bar reporting are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for EigenScore, random controls, ESU steering, and the 70B model. Table 3 additionally reports overall hallucination rates: for Qwen on TriviaQA, the post-calibration overall rate is 34.4%, versus 23.4% confident hallucinations. Previously reported table values are retained. The headline reduction changes from 31.9% to 29.6% across an expanded model set, so this is not a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the informal VU definition with VU(U|C) = 1 − Pr(P|U,C), interpreted through a listener's subjective probability, and specifies an ordering between answers. Section 3.1 also adds the normalized-vector equation. These are limited formal-definition additions.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the headline reduction claim from hallucinations generally to confident hallucinations. The three central contributions—linear VUF discovery, combined-uncertainty detection, and MUC steering—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 attributes Qwen's lower steering sensitivity to larger embedding norms under normalized VUFs, discusses potential judge circularity, and explains correctness losses through semantic-entropy noise causing false abstentions (Sections 3.2 and 4.2; Appendix G.3). The existing short-form QA and generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, the exact accuracy-judge prompt in Appendix A.3, full ESU/EUU prototype-expression lists in Appendix E.2, and the 70B intervention cap of 4.0 in Appendix G.1. These substantially expand the implementation and measurement information available for reproduction.

R1.justification: The research bibliography, related-work discussions in Sections 2.4 and 5, and positioning relative to prior approaches are unchanged. The added terminology footnote does not revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the uncertainty definitions, reorganizes Section 3.2 around effective-layer selection, clarifies terminology, and gives existing appendix examples descriptive headings. The overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 gain comparator columns, metric columns, or experimental rows. Qwen plot axes are extended, Figure 13 is added, and existing figures are relocated, including the exchange of Figures 4 and 5. The underlying visual style and most displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in validating and communicating the central result. Random-direction controls and ESU-based causal validation strengthen attribution to VUF steering. Separating overall from confident hallucinations corrects the ambiguity in v1's headline and table labeling, while Appendix G.3 explains the correctness–abstention tradeoff. Together with substantially improved reproduction information, these provide meaningful gains in evidential strength and transparency despite the method's retained accuracy tradeoff.
